preconditions.expression: n >= 2 and 1 <= r1 < r2 <= n and r1 != r2
preconditions.description: Input consists of n cities (2 ≤ n ≤ 50000), old capital r1, and new capital r2 (1 ≤ r1 ≠ r2 ≤ n), with r2 strictly greater than r1 to avoid ambiguity in path reconstruction.

preconditions.expression: len(p) == n - 1 and all(1 <= pi <= n for pi in p) and all(pi != i for i, pi in enumerate(p, start=2))
preconditions.description: The old representation p is a list of n-1 integers (one per city except r1), where each pi is the parent of city i+1 in the original tree rooted at r1. No city is its own parent.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= i <= n for i in range(1, n + 1))
preconditions.description: City indices are integers from 1 to n inclusive.

postconditions.expression: len(new_p) == n - 1 and all(1 <= new_pi <= n for new_pi in new_p)
postconditions.description: Output is a list of n-1 integers, each representing the new parent of a city (excluding r2) in the tree rooted at r2.

postconditions.expression: all(new_pi != i for i, new_pi in enumerate(new_p, start=2))
postconditions.description: No city is its own parent in the new representation.

postconditions.expression: all(any(new_p[j] == i for j in range(n - 1) if j + 2 == i) for i in range(1, n + 1) if i != r2)
postconditions.description: For every city i ≠ r2, there exists exactly one entry in new_p where new_p[j] = i, meaning i is the parent of some city in the new tree.

postconditions.expression: all(any(new_p[j] == k for j in range(n - 1) if j + 2 == k) for k in range(1, n + 1) if k != r2)
postconditions.description: Every city k ≠ r2 appears as a parent in new_p exactly once (if it has children in the new tree).

postconditions.expression: all(not any(new_p[j] == i for j in range(n - 1) if j + 2 == i) for i in range(1, n + 1) if i == r2)
postconditions.description: The new capital r2 does not appear as a child in new_p (it has no parent).

postconditions.expression: all(any(new_p[j] == i for j in range(n - 1) if j + 2 == k) for k in range(1, n + 1) if k != r2) or (k == r2 and not any(new_p[j] == i for j in range(n - 1) if j + 2 == k))
postconditions.description: The new tree is valid: every city k ≠ r2 has exactly one parent in new_p, and r2 has no parent.

postconditions.expression: all(any(new_p[j] == i for j in range(n - 1) if j + 2 == k) for k in range(1, n + 1) if k != r2) and all(not any(new_p[j] == i for j in range(n - 1) if j + 2 == k) for k in range(1, n + 1) if k == r2)
postconditions.description: The new representation correctly defines a tree rooted at r2, where every city (except r2) has exactly one parent, and r2 is the root.

postconditions.expression: all(not any(new_p[j] == i for j in range(n - 1) if j + 2 == k) for k in range(1, n + 1) if k == r2)
postconditions.description: The new capital r2 is not listed as a child in new_p (it is the root).

postconditions.expression: all(new_p[j] != r2 for j in range(n - 1) if j + 2 != r2)
postconditions.description: The new capital r2 is not a parent of any city except possibly itself (which is impossible).

postconditions.expression: all(new_p[j] == i for j in range(n - 1) if j + 2 == k) if (k != r2 and k != r1) else True
postconditions.description: For cities k ≠ r2 and k ≠ r1, the parent in new_p is the same as in the original tree if the path from r1 to k does not pass through r2.

postconditions.expression: all(new_p[j] == r2 for j in range(n - 1) if j + 2 == k and k != r2 and k != r1 and any(p[i] == r2 for i in range(n - 1) if i + 2 == k))
postconditions.description: For cities k ≠ r2 and k ≠ r1, if the path from r1 to k passes through r2, then the new parent of k is r2.

postconditions.expression: all(new_p[j] == r2 for j in range(n - 1) if j + 2 == r1)
postconditions.description: The old capital r1's new parent is r2.
